source: 5 AAC 09 (Alaska Peninsula Area), Article 2 (Salmon Fishery: districts, sections and subdistricts) and Article 3 (closed waters); the corresponding printed booklet is the 2026-2029 Alaska Peninsula, Atka-Amlia Islands, Aleutian Islands, and Chignik Areas Commercial Salmon Fishing Regulations
notation: degrees and decimal minutes, e.g. "55° 33.98' N. lat." / "159° 35.88' W. long." — NOT degrees-minutes-seconds. lat_dm/lon_dm hold the value EXACTLY as printed, unconverted, including the source's inconsistent degree sign: 5 AAC 09.200 and parts of 09.350 use ° (U+00B0) while many 09.350 items use º (U+00BA, masculine ordinal). Two coordinates are printed as whole degrees with no minutes at all — Cape Newenham "162° W. long." in 09.200(a) and Little Bear Bay "162º W. long." in 09.350(25)(B) — and are recorded that way; they are not degrees+minutes and will not parse as such. Decimal conversion is degrees + minutes/60, negative for west longitude.
source_document_caveat: The ADF&G booklet named in source_url could not be read directly: this session's egress policy blocks downloading it, and the fetch relay returns only summaries of PDFs. All text here was therefore transcribed from two independent published mirrors of the codified regulation — Cornell LII and Justia — listed in text_retrieved_from. Both mirrors derive from the same state codification, so their agreement proves faithful transcription, not independent authority. Currency: the Cornell history note for 5 AAC 09.200 ends "am 5/30/2007, Register 182" and for 5 AAC 09.350 ends "am 6/5/2016, Register 218, July 2016"; neither page shows a current-through date. Any Board of Fisheries amendment after those dates, and any emergency order, is NOT reflected here. Verify against the printed booklet before fishing.
verification_method: Every area was read twice, by two differently-worded fetches, in every case across two different hosts (Cornell LII and Justia). Only values identical in both reads are recorded with verified_twice=true. Two coordinate pairs were elided by one host's first read (the second point of Inner Port Heiden Section, 5 AAC 09.200(a)(2)(B), and the base of Trader Mountain, 5 AAC 09.350(16)(B)); each was recovered by a third, narrowly worded read of the host that had dropped it, and matched the other host's read digit for digit. Every decimal value was recomputed by hand as degrees + minutes/60, negated for west longitude, and checked against the Alaska Peninsula envelope lat 54-59, lon -170 to -156. No coordinate in this file was supplied from any source other than the two mirrors; landmarks named without a printed coordinate carry lat_dm/lon_dm = null even where the same landmark's coordinate appears in another paragraph.
structure_notes: 5 AAC 09.200 has exactly six lettered subsections: (a) Northern, (b) Northwestern, (c) Unimak, (d) Southwestern, (e) South Central, (f) Southeastern. There is NO "Bering Sea District" in this section — both hosts confirm the phrase "Bering Sea" appears only as the geographic descriptor in the Northern and Northwestern District descriptions. 5 AAC 09.350 is titled "Closed waters" and reads "Salmon may not be taken in the following locations:" followed by a flat list numbered (1) through (37) with no lettered subsections; because that list is not organised by district, most closures here carry parent=null. parent is set only where the closure text itself names a section.

No coordinates are involved -- this closure is defined entirely by a vegetation line and a landmark, so nothing here can be plotted.

areas.text: Balboa Bay: (A) waters north of a line extending west from Reef Point
areas.notes: Reef Point is named without a coordinate; the closure line is unplottable from the regulation text alone.

areas.name: Balboa Bay — Lefthand Bay
areas.text: Balboa Bay: (B) waters of Lefthand Bay west of a line from 55º 31.60' N. lat., 160º 43.00' W. long. to 55º 33.10' N. lat., 160º 42.10' W. long.

areas.name: San Diego Bay
areas.text: San Diego Bay: waters of the lagoon at the head of this bay and within 500 yards outside of the lagoon's entrance, except that from July 19 through August 31 the closure includes all waters west of a line from the reef at 55º 33.10' N. lat., 160º 26.60' W. long. to the headland at 55º 33.97' N. lat., 160º 25.90' W. long.

areas.name: Dorenoi Bay — after July 25
areas.text: Dorenoi Bay: (B) after July 25, waters within 500 yards of the terminus of any salmon stream
areas.notes: Paragraph (32)(A) was repealed 6/2/2010 and is not recorded here.

areas.name: Chichagof Bay
areas.text: Chichagof Bay: waters of the lagoon and within 500 yards of the lagoon entrance

areas.name: Orzinski Bay (Orzenoi)
areas.text: Orzinski Bay (Orzenoi): waters within 1,000 yards of any salmon stream

areas.name: Grub Gulch
areas.text: Grub Gulch: waters north of 55° 48.25' N. lat.
areas.notes: A bare latitude cutoff with no printed east/west limit. Parent left null on purpose: this closure lies north of the latitude range spanned by the Southeastern District's own two boundary landmarks, so bounding it by that district's coordinate envelope would erase it.

areas.name: Stepovak Bay — June 1 through July 28
areas.text: Stepovak Bay: (A) from June 1 through July 28, waters within 500 yards of any salmon stream or lagoon, unless otherwise specified in this chapter

areas.name: Stepovak Bay — July 29 through September 30
areas.text: Stepovak Bay: (B) from July 29 through September 30, waters north of a line extending east from Dent Point at 55° 47.25' N. lat., 159° 52.00' W. long. to a point on the Kupreanof Peninsula at 55° 46.93' N. lat., 159° 38.70' W. long.
areas.notes: Dent Point's longitude here, 159° 52.00' W., is the same value 5 AAC 09.200(f)(5)-(f)(7) use for the longitude of Dent Point -- an internal confirmation of the digits.

areas.name: East Stepovak Section — July 6 through August 31
areas.text: from July 6 through August 31, waters of Alaska in the East Stepovak Section between a line extending 135° from Kupreanof Point at 55° 33.98' N. lat., 159° 35.88' W. long. and a line extending 207° from 55° 34.50' N. lat., 159° 37.53' W. long.; from September 1 through September 30, the commissioner shall close, by emergency order, the waters specified in this paragraph when the waters specified in 5 AAC 15.350(20) are closed to conserve coho salmon.
areas.notes: Kupreanof Point's coordinates here match 5 AAC 09.200(f)(3), (f)(7) and the (f) district description exactly. The September 1-30 half of this paragraph is a conditional emergency-order closure, not a standing one.
